subject: English
passage: Although most temperate tree species have relatively thin outer bark, some species develop unusually thick, corky bark that can insulate living tissue from intense heat. Many dendrologists have assumed that thick bark would shield trunks during wildfires and thus would allow species that develop it to have higher post-fire survival rates than species with thin bark do. To evaluate this assumption, a research team led by fire ecologist Nils Colombo and dendrologist Mpho Benali analyzed records for more than 2,400 tree species across fire-prone regions.
prompt: Which finding from Colombo and Benali's study, if true, would most directly challenge the assumption in the underlined sentence?

choices.A: Species with thin bark tend to have slower annual growth rates than species with thick bark.
choices.B: Species with thin bark tend to have smaller average leaf areas than species with thick bark.
choices.C: Species with thin bark tend to have lighter-colored bark than species with thick bark do.
choices.D: Species with thin bark tend to have higher post-fire survival rates than species with thick bark.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would directly challenge the assumption described in the underlined sentence. The text explains that many dendrologists have assumed that because thick bark shields trunks during wildfires, tree species with thick bark should have higher post-fire survival rates than species with thin bark. If Colombo and Benali found instead that species with thin bark tend to have higher post-fire survival rates than species with thick bark, that finding would show the opposite of what the dendrologists assumed and would therefore undermine their assumption.
